title: Draw a clinker-style comparison of gene clusters
summary: Align five aminoglycoside gene clusters on one shared gene and link similar proteins with LOSATP similarity groups.
primaryWorkflow: Compare gene clusters by protein similarity

requirements: Select Linear mode and add the clusters. Open gbdraw.app, select Linear, and add the five clusters in this order. Reverse-complement the last one so that all five read in the same direction. Row: 1, GenBank / DDBJ File: BGC0000708.gbk, Reverse complement: No; Row: 2, GenBank / DDBJ File: BGC0000709.gbk, Reverse complement: No; Row: 3, GenBank / DDBJ File: BGC0000711.gbk, Reverse complement: No; Row: 4, GenBank / DDBJ File: BGC0000712.gbk, Reverse complement: No; Row: 5, GenBank / DDBJ File: BGC0000713.gbk, Reverse complement: Yes.

Group similar proteins. Under Pairwise Comparisons choose Run LOSAT and LOSATP, set LOSATP mode to Similarity groups, and set Min identity (%) to 30. clinker aligns all clusters against each other in the same way and links members of a group. Set the alignment gene to CAF33315.1, which aligns the clusters on its group. Control: LOSAT Mode, Value: LOSATP; Control: LOSATP mode, Value: Similarity groups; Control: Min identity (%), Value: 30; Control: Alignment feature, Value: CAF33315.1.

Color the genes. Load the two color tables. gbdraw colors genes by rule, not by group: the four gene_kind rules give core biosynthetic, additional biosynthetic, transport, and regulatory genes their own colors, and the link between members shows the group. Control: Default colors, Value: BGC0000708-BGC0000713_default_colors.tsv; Control: Specific rules, Value: BGC0000708-BGC0000713_specific_colors.tsv; Control: Show Labels, Value: First Record Only; Control: Scale Style, Value: Bar (Simple); Control: Legend position, Value: Bottom.

Generate and read the figure. Click Generate Diagram. Links shade from pale to saturated red with identity. A run of core biosynthetic genes links through all five clusters, while regulatory genes occur only in the two neomycin clusters. Links show protein similarity, not orthology.
